identity.name: Pasha de Cartier

case.bezel: smooth bezel beneath a screw-down crown-protector cap on a chain

identity.one_liner: A round case with a screw-down crown-protector cap on a small chain, Cartier's own solution to water resistance before screw-down crowns became the industry standard.

narrative.story: Cartier's own account traces the Pasha's design to a 1943 commission from the Pasha of Marrakech, who reportedly wanted a wristwatch he could swim in; Cartier did not launch the Pasha de Cartier as a catalog watch line until 1985, built around a screw-down cap that locks over the crown and attaches to the case by a small chain. Cartier refreshed the collection again in 2020, keeping the chained crown cap as the model's clearest visual signature.
narrative.collector_notes: This reference (WHPA0018) is a skeletonized rose gold automatic on caliber 9624 MC, part of Cartier's current Pasha lineup, which is presently offered in precious metals rather than steel in Cartier's US catalog; the crown-protector chain is a specific wear point, so check that it is intact and threads smoothly without cross-threading.
